facts: The first factory began with dedicated forward and return rail routes.
Shared return capacity was introduced while forward routes stayed dedicated, creating difficult-to-read spaghetti.
The limited Rotor, Stator, and Applicator factory remained reliable and was deliberately left operating rather than rebuilt.
Its buffered exports did not starve the later Faraday factory.
Ore and ingots stayed on dedicated routes while Plate, Wire, Powder, and higher products shared a global loop.
The one-input, select-output, return-to-bus workflow was unusually enjoyable and productive.
As the loop grew, shortcuts and direct high-volume bypasses created multiple opaque paths and the network slowed or stopped pulling correctly.
After roughly two hours of unsuccessful diagnosis, the player tore down every machine in the second factory.
checkpoints.hypothesis_not_fact: The player suspected a game routing bug, but the prompts do not establish whether the stoppage was a bug, hidden contention, request starvation, or a connection error.

facts: The intermediate design used dedicated Ore and ingot feeds, separate elemental shape buses, and one low-volume U-shaped central bus.
Mixed-element recipes were grouped into clusters with long extensions from the relevant elemental buses.
Ceramics fed storage and then Synthetic Silicon directly; slack Ceramics could serve secondary users.
The player wanted expensive Chemicals and Acid centralized when practical, while recognizing their refill waves could congest a shared 480/min trunk.
checkpoints.status_note: This records the design path. The U-bus experiment is not the final canonical Faraday topology.

facts: The completed hybrid used two Cores plus Amplifiers, one bounded low-volume bus, separate Titanium, Calcium, and Helium networks, and two Wolfram networks.
A direct Chemicals to Sulphuric Acid feed kept the dominant Chemicals flow off the shared bus.
The layout was visually messier but easy to trace and ran for hours while storage was repeatedly emptied as a stress test.
The outbound yard had twelve Storage Depot v2 units.
At a later exploration checkpoint, every product then craftable had been turned in and there was no useful construction left before obtaining more blueprints.
The player spent about three hours optimizing Faraday until the factory ran at line speed.
A second Supermagnet Furnace was then installed as burst and recovery capacity despite the possibility of Acid-limited simultaneous demand.

facts: A pure Titanium source and merged pairs of Helium and Sulfur sources were each limited by the serving rail to roughly one source of flow.

The player described the desired upgrade as Rail v4, but canonical Update 1 data calls the 480/min player-facing tier Rail v3; the observed bottleneck is retained while the literal tier is unresolved.
Ore Excavator v2 was not owned at this transcript checkpoint.
Long-distance rails ended at storage yards and did not enter internal factory networks.
Titanium Rod and Wolfram Plate were rejected as world-bus or export-yard cargo.
Ammunition and building-material Cargo Dispatchers were being considered for temporary expedition firebases and Geo Scanner assaults.

checkpoints.relative_phase: current live exploration after Little Cloud
facts: The first Geo Scanner defense was completed after two deaths and a third, successful attempt.
The first death respawned the player at a nearby claimed base, but that base had no replacement weapons or materials, forcing a walk back to Landerworks.
For the second attempt, the player claimed the Regeneration Chamber at a temporary scanner fire base but forgot or did not realize that the installed turrets required power.
The unpowered turrets did nothing, the player was overwhelmed, and corruption disabled the base and took its Regeneration Chamber offline.
The second death therefore respawned the player at the starting launcher rather than at the intended fire-base checkpoint.
The successful attempt used a fully built-out fire base with all turrets powered.
The powered automated defense was highly satisfying; the player described listening to the turrets singing against the enemy.
After completion, the player sorted loot and gear and continued exploring toward the next major fight.
checkpoints.unresolved_observation: The site appeared to yield two particularly good food-related rewards or stacks, possibly involving a quantity of 20, but the dictated item names/counts were ambiguous.

incidents_and_observations.observation: After a large teardown, cargo drones remained floating in the air and survived save/reload.
The player accidentally drew aggro near Copperfield, ran out of ammunition, could not disengage, and died.
incidents_and_observations.lesson: Treat high-threat named sites as deliberate raids with an abort route and ammunition reserve, not casual scanner stops.

incidents_and_observations.observation: Two failed Geo Scanner attempts exposed an empty nearby respawn base and a corruption-disabled fire-base Regeneration Chamber before a powered-turret third attempt succeeded.
lessons: A nearby claimed respawn is not a useful recovery point unless it stocks replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials.
Installed turrets must be powered and function-checked before scanner activation.
Do not keep the only recovery cache inside the same contested base whose corruption can disable the Regeneration Chamber.
Plan the worst-case respawn and return route before beginning a major defense.
incidents_and_observations.mechanic_boundary: This encounter directly demonstrates the observed failure sequence, but does not establish the universal corruption threshold or every condition that disables a Regeneration Chamber.

incidents_and_observations.observation: A lake crossed by a rail and zipline, but no Platforms, continued to spawn substantial forage.
incidents_and_observations.boundary: This contradicts a blanket nearby-structure suppression rule but does not test Platform effects.

incidents_and_observations.observation: The player reported that Figler was unlocked and that nothing was left afterward.
incidents_and_observations.verified_context: The structured model lists 30 Prickler and 100 Data Points as research inputs, then models the finished Figler as a separate Food Station craft using 3 Prickler.

production_and_time: Do not optimize for continuous steady state alone; model finite campaigns separated by hours away from the factory.
Do not use large storage as a substitute for adequate productive capacity.
Strategic stockpiling during active play is welcome; AFK-only completion is not.
For below-level-12 turn-ins, target under one hour and allow up to two hours only rarely.
For later final campaigns, one to two hours is preferred; an occasional three to four hours is tolerable.
A few modest specialist factories are fun; rebuilding the same large dependency chain repeatedly is tedious.
Cheap extraction may be deliberately overbuilt for cold-start recovery when the alternative is a large, hot duplicate processing chain.
buffers: At the later planning checkpoint, V2 storage was used for later-stage parts rather than raw Ore.
A mature route is effectively triple buffered by machine output storage, source-yard V2 storage, and destination-yard V2 storage.
New products often begin at zero while their inputs are already warm and buffered.
architecture: Prefer debuggable tree-shaped freight and visible interfaces over opaque rail meshes.
Terminate world freight at storage yards.
Keep high-rate raw and shape products local; move compact intermediates between specialist sites.
Split recommendations by base and campus so space, rail lanes, and Core heat can be reserved before construction.
Logical campus separation can remain useful even when physical Cores are spread farther apart to reduce heat and concentrated attacks.
recipe_selection: Offer owned V2 buildings as recipe options rather than forcing them blindly.
Compare V1 and V2 choices using onsite inputs, distance, heat, freight, footprint, and batch size.
exploration_and_combat: Use conservative, low-twitch combat plans calibrated to the player's self-reported FPS constraint.
Optimize resource and expedition routes for understandability, defense, expansion, and debuggability rather than nearest distance alone.
Track multiple goals together so food, map, blueprint, War Bond, and resource needs are not lost when the conversation shifts.
Prefer compact one-slot expedition food that covers both hunger and hydration.
communication: Use plain English, exact machine counts, visible math, and explicit assumptions.
Stress-test a proposed architecture rather than approving it merely because it matches the player's initial idea.
Preserve reopenable visualizations and the reasoning behind plan changes.
